GK-07.c01: Driving too fast is a **major cause of fatal crashes**.
Your speed must fit **five things**: traction (tire grip), curves, visibility, traffic, and hills.
GK-07.c02: Total stopping distance = perception + reaction + braking distance: at 55 mph ≈ **142 + 61 + 216 = 419 ft**, a minimum under ideal conditions.
Perception takes about **1¾ seconds** and reaction ¾ to 1 second; during both you are still rolling at full speed.
Double the speed → impact and braking distance **4 times** greater (triple → 9, quadruple → 16); empty trucks need **longer** stopping distances because they have less traction.
[CA] Service brakes must hold the vehicle still on any grade, loaded or empty, and stop it from **20 mph** within a maximum stopping distance.
[CA] Limits from 20 mph: car 25 ft; single under 10,000 lb 30 ft; single 10,000 lb or more, any bus, light vehicle towing 40 ft; other combinations **50 ft**.
GK-07.c03: Traction is the friction between tires and road; without it you **cannot steer or brake**.
Wet roads can double stopping distance → slow about **one-third** (55 → about 35 mph); packed snow → slow **half or more**; ice → crawl, stop when safe.
Watch for shaded areas, bridges (freeze **before the road**; take care near 32°F), melting ice, **black ice** (road just looks wet), and the first rain mixing with oil.
Hydroplaning can happen as low as **30 mph**; release the accelerator and push in the clutch, and **do not brake**.
GK-07.c04: Too fast in a curve → the tires lose traction and you **skid off the road**, or they keep traction and the vehicle **rolls over**.
**Slow down before** entering the curve, because braking inside it can lock the wheels and start a skid.
Never exceed the posted curve speed, and be in a gear that lets you **accelerate slightly** through the curve for control.
GK-07.c05: Your stopping distance must always fit **inside the distance you can see ahead**.
Fog, rain or other conditions that cut visibility → slow down.
At night, **low beams** show less road than high beams, so slow down when using them.
GK-07.c06: In heavy traffic, the safest speed is **the same speed as the vehicles around you**, if legal and safe.
[CA] Truck and bus speed limits are lower than car limits, by **as much as 15 mph**, so take extra care changing lanes or passing.
Speeding to save time saves very little; constant passing raises **crash risk** and fatigue.
GK-07.c07: Pick a speed that fits total weight, grade length, grade steepness, road conditions, and weather; never exceed a **"Maximum Safe Speed"** or posted limit.
**Engine braking** is your main speed control, strongest near governed rpm in a lower gear; save the service brakes for slowing or stopping.
**Shift to a low gear before** starting down the grade, so you have full engine braking from the top.
GK-07.c08: **Speeding traffic** is the number one cause of injuries and deaths in work zones.
Obey the posted work-zone speed limit and watch your speedometer so speed doesn't **creep up** in long construction areas.
Slow down for bad weather or road conditions, and **even more** when a worker is close to the road.
GK-07.c09: [CA] Outside business or residential districts, pass a vehicle going under **20 mph** on a grade only if at least **10 mph faster** and finishing within ¼ mile.
[CA] Stay at least **300 feet** behind trucks with 3+ axles, vehicles towing, school buses with pupils, farm labor vehicles, explosives carriers, and trailer buses.
[CA] The 300-foot rule does not apply while passing, where there are **2 or more lanes** each way, or in business or residential districts.
[CA] Large vehicles traveling in a caravan on open highway must leave at least **100 feet** between them so others can pass.
